title: From Chennai to Japan, Rajinikanth Fans Turn Jailer 2 Opening Into a Festival
excerpt: Garlanded cut-outs, 3 AM full houses in Dubai, temple rituals in Madurai and a first-ever same-day Japan release marked the superstar's return as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian on October 15.
body:
• Rajinikanth fans turned Jailer 2's October 15 opening into a festival across Chennai, Bengaluru, Dubai, Singapore, Japan and North America, with garlanded cut-outs, firecrackers and packed early-morning shows.
  • Jailer 2 is the first Rajinikanth film to open in India and Japan on the same day, and Japanese fans marked it with custom merchandise and social media countdowns.
  • In Madurai, fans performed temple rituals including angapradakshinam at the Veyil Vandha Amman Temple in Tirupparankundram, praying for the film's success and Rajinikanth's health.
  • The sequel, directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, follows the 2023 hit Jailer, which grossed about Rs 604 crore worldwide.

Rajinikanth's fans did not wait for the reviews. Long before sunrise on Thursday, October 15, the opening of Jailer 2 had become a street festival across continents — garlanded cut-outs, firecrackers, temple prayers and housefull early-morning shows from Chennai to Dubai, Singapore, Japan and North America, as the superstar returned to the screen as 'Tiger' Muthuvel Pandian.

A carnival that started before dawn

In Dubai, theatres at Deira City Centre were full by 3 AM, with crowds chanting Rajinikanth's name into the early hours, The Daily Jagran reported. In Bengaluru, fans set off rounds of fireworks before the 6:30 AM shows, offered prayers and broke coconuts outside theatres, where tall cut-outs stood covered in flower garlands. Chennai's Rohini Silver Screens saw long queues and housefull boards, and in Attur, in Salem district, fans used a crane to garland a 30-foot cut-out of Rajinikanth outside a theatre, performed a traditional milk abhishekam and burst firecrackers.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2110552591084212574

The celebrations were devotional as well as festive. In Madurai, fans performed special rituals at the Veyil Vandha Amman Temple in Tirupparankundram, including mann soru — eating food directly from the ground as part of a religious vow — and angapradakshinam, rolling around the temple premises as an act of devotion, according to ANI reporting carried by Devdiscourse. Fans also created a Navaratri Kolu at the Rajini Temple featuring more than 230 of his iconic film characters. Speaking to PTI Videos, Chennai fan Ravi said he had watched Rajinikanth's films since childhood and hoped the sequel would do better than the original.

Japan's same-day first, and the diaspora shows

Jailer 2 is the first Rajinikanth film to open in India and Japan on the same day. Japanese fans shared videos of custom merchandise ahead of the release, and fan accounts counted down to what they called a historic same-day opening. In Singapore, fans filled cinemas for the early shows and lit the dark with phone torches. In Canada, cinema lobbies were packed, and in the US fans danced outside theatres, with fan clubs in New Jersey saying all the early shows were full and moviegoers welcomed by life-size cut-outs and balloons.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XmNmf1emnvY

A day before the release, Rajinikanth's daughter, director Soundarya Rajinikanth, unveiled a promotional LED banner at Kashi Theatre in Chennai and joined fans in dancing to a song from the first Jailer.

The film fans are celebrating

Jailer 2 is a rare Rajinikanth sequel. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, it continues the story of the 2023 blockbuster Jailer, in which retired prison warden Muthuvel Pandian was pulled back into violence. In the sequel, Pandian's quieter family life is disrupted again as a cross-border criminal syndicate threatens his family, and he works from the shadows — including going undercover as a driver — to break it. Anirudh Ravichander returns as composer.

The cast extends well beyond the lead. Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu and Mirnaa return, joined by Vidya Balan, Mithun Chakraborty, Jackie Shroff and Suraj Venjaramoodu, with cameo appearances by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar and Hrithik Roshan. The original Jailer grossed about Rs 604 crore worldwide, and the sequel opened amid a separate box-office storyline — advance bookings of about Rs 38 crore and a revenue-sharing dispute over the Hindi release — that The Videshi has covered separately.

Where diaspora readers can watch

Jailer 2 is in theatres now, released worldwide on October 15. Diaspora readers will find it in the usual Tamil-release circuits: major chains and independent screens across the US and Canada — where opening shows in New Jersey were reported full — the Gulf, Singapore and, for the first time for a Rajinikanth film on day one, Japan. Given the reported sell-outs of early shows, booking ahead rather than walking in is the practical advice for opening weekend.
